decisions.reason: The Statement asserts unique local solutions through each consistent initial pair, not a separate smooth-dependence theorem. Steps 1.1–1.2 extend the explicit multiplier to an open full-rank neighborhood, where the field is smooth and Picard–Lindelof applies. Step 1.3 proves invariance: the derivative of J M^{-1}p is zero identically and dc/dt is its initially zero value. Uniqueness follows in step 2.1. The autonomous solution family also obeys the local flow composition law by uniqueness of time-translated solutions; a common local time near any fixed initial pair follows from boundedness and Lipschitz bounds on a smaller closed ball in the open ambient domain. No uniform time over unbounded momenta is claimed. The title does not invalidate the proved Statement.

The opening clause restricts the entire Statement to the selected local branch, not to arbitrary roots or a continuation to all regular endpoints. The definition specifies the branch through the h=0 multiplier center, and the branch lemma supplies jointly smooth local roots. In proof 1.2–2.1, swapping the forward multipliers recovers exactly the original half-momentum, position, and momentum. As (h,z) tends to (0,z0), the endpoint tends to z0 and the swapped multipliers tend to its common branch center. Thus shrinking the local domain puts the reverse input and both swapped multipliers in the joint IFT uniqueness neighborhood; uniqueness identifies the reverse selected step. Repeating with -h proves the other composition, and h=0 is the identity. Shrinking a germ-local branch domain is legitimate in this local assertion. Endpoint regularity alone would not establish a global continuation claim, but no such claim is made. The cited paper’s Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.9 likewise use local uniqueness for small steps.

The dependency includes its proof, not only its Statement. Proof 1.1 of thm-rattle-scaled-solve-residual-error-budget explicitly derives ||lambda_tilde-lambda|| <= 2||A(q)^{-1}|| epsilon_q, and proof 2.2 uses the inverse of A(q_tilde_1) for the momentum root. Therefore F2 accurately identifies the inverse-matrix bounds used by that theorem. Independently, the displayed constant Jacobian has Gram trace 2+epsilon^2 and determinant epsilon^2, yielding exactly the stated eigenvalues and lambda_min/epsilon^2 -> 1/2. Since the scaled position equation for this linear constraint family is affine with multiplier derivative -A_epsilon, a unit residual in a smallest-eigenvalue direction requires multiplier error 1/lambda_min. Thus the residual-to-multiplier bound really is nonuniform. The item claims multiplier conditioning, not that every possible state-error estimate must diverge at that same rate; epsilon=0 correctly fails rank.

F1 is specialized to the given circle constraint, not asserted for arbitrary constraints. Here J(q)=q^T and c(q)=0 implies ||q||=ell>0, so rank J(q)=1 automatically. Consequently c(q)=0 together with q^T M^{-1}p=0 is exactly consistency in this example; no regularity hypothesis is lost. Direct substitution of lambda=mu=m omega^2/(1+sqrt(1-h^2 omega^2)) gives both displayed updates, exact norm ell, and q1^T p1=0. This root has the required half-continuous-multiplier limit and stays separated from the other position root throughout 0<h omega<=1/2. The continuous circle trajectory satisfies the equations with multiplier m omega^2. Taylor expansion of arcsin on an open interval containing [0,1/2] gives its bounded cubic remainder and the claimed O(h^3) phase defect for fixed omega.
